shortDescription: Nordic forward power prices rose to their highest levels since January 2023 on Wednesday, supported by soaring European gas prices.

children: Nordic forward power prices rose to their highest levels since January 2023 on Wednesday, supported by soaring European gas prices.
The Nordic front-quarter baseload power contract (NSBLQc1) was up €4.85, or 5.21%, at €97.9 per megawatt hour (MWh) at 0955 GMT, its highest since January 2023.
Nordic front-year (NSBLYc1) rose €1.91, or 3.28%, to €60.1 per MWh, hitting a more than three-year high.
"Massive price increases in gas and German power, where panic is growing ahead of the heating season, are driving up Nordic futures," Mind Energy analysts said in a note.
Dutch and British gas prices also rose, with the benchmark Dutch contract touching a 43-month high as the United States and Iran exchanged strikes overnight.
European benchmark front-year electricity contracts climbed further in early trading, tracking higher gas prices.
Nordic water reserves available 15 days ahead (PCAEC00) were seen at 13.43 terawatt hours (TWh) below normal, compared with 10.62 TWh below normal on Tuesday.
"Temperatures will be mostly below normal, accompanied by above-normal rain. The week after next week could be less active," said LSEG meteorologist Georg Muller.
Germany's year-ahead power (TRDEBYc1), Europe's benchmark contract, rose €3.95, or 3.3%, to €123.8 per MWh.
